notes: Curated baseline for gameplay and research; not an exhaustive historical record.
game_relevance and economic_sectors are interpretive metadata, not claims of measured market impact.
Month-precision entries use YYYY-MM when an exact day is intentionally not asserted.
Before using an event for deterministic market simulation, validate it against market/price datasets separately.

fed_great_inflation.name: The Great Inflation - Federal Reserve History

nber_cycle.name: Business Cycle Dating Committee Announcements - NBER

events.headline: U.S. announces grain embargo against Soviet Union
events.summary: President Jimmy Carter restricts grain exports to the USSR following the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.

events.headline: Silver prices reach an extraordinary peak
events.summary: Silver prices surge amid the Hunt brothers' attempt to corner the market, becoming a signature commodity-market episode of the era.

events.headline: Pittsburgh Steelers win Super Bowl XIV
events.summary: The Steelers defeat the Los Angeles Rams 31-19, becoming the first NFL franchise to win four Super Bowls.

events.headline: Lake Placid Winter Olympics open
events.summary: The XIII Olympic Winter Games open in Lake Placid, New York, amid intense Cold War attention.

events.headline: Miracle on Ice
events.summary: The U.S. Olympic hockey team defeats the heavily favored Soviet team in the medal round at Lake Placid.

events.headline: High inflation and tight money dominate the U.S. economy
events.summary: The Volcker Federal Reserve continues an aggressive anti-inflation policy as borrowing costs remain extremely high.

events.headline: Carter administration imposes credit controls
events.summary: The administration introduces credit restraints as part of the fight against inflation, contributing to a sharp pullback in borrowing and spending.

events.headline: Depository Institutions Deregulation and Monetary Control Act signed
events.summary: The law changes banking regulation and expands Federal Reserve requirements across depository institutions.

events.headline: Mount St. Helens activity intensifies
events.summary: Earthquakes and steam explosions at Mount St. Helens signal the volcanic crisis that will culminate in May.

events.headline: Operation Eagle Claw fails in Iran
events.summary: A U.S. attempt to rescue hostages in Iran is aborted after mechanical problems and a deadly collision in the desert.

events.headline: 1980 recession deepens
events.summary: Tight credit, high interest rates, and falling activity push the U.S. economy into a sharp but brief recession.

events.headline: Arcade gaming expands rapidly
events.summary: The U.S. arcade-game boom accelerates, setting the stage for Pac-Man and other major releases to become mass-market cultural phenomena.

events.headline: WHO certifies eradication of smallpox
events.summary: The World Health Organization formally declares smallpox eradicated worldwide.

events.headline: Mount St. Helens erupts catastrophically
events.summary: The Washington volcano erupts, killing dozens and causing widespread environmental and economic damage.

events.headline: The Empire Strikes Back reaches theaters
events.summary: The second released Star Wars film becomes one of the year's defining entertainment events.

events.headline: CNN launches as a 24-hour news network
events.summary: Cable News Network begins broadcasting, introducing continuous television news coverage.

events.headline: 1980 recession nears its trough
events.summary: The brief 1980 downturn reaches its low point around midyear; NBER later dates the trough to July.

events.headline: Severe U.S. heat wave begins
events.summary: A prolonged heat wave affects much of the central and southern United States, causing major loss of life and agricultural stress.

events.headline: Ronald Reagan wins Republican presidential nomination
events.summary: The Republican convention nominates Reagan for president, setting the general-election contest against Jimmy Carter.

events.headline: Moscow Summer Olympics begin
events.summary: The Olympics open in Moscow under the shadow of a U.S.-led boycott following the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.

events.headline: Unemployment rises as the recession bottoms
events.summary: U.S. unemployment reaches a four-year high while economic activity approaches the recession trough.

events.headline: Jimmy Carter wins Democratic renomination
events.summary: President Carter secures the Democratic nomination after defeating Senator Ted Kennedy's primary challenge.

events.headline: Solidarity movement gains recognition in Poland
events.summary: The Gdansk Agreement recognizes independent trade unions, giving rise to Solidarity as a major challenge to communist rule.

events.headline: Economic recovery begins after short recession
events.summary: Activity begins recovering from the 1980 recession even as inflation remains high and monetary policy stays volatile.

events.headline: Iran-Iraq War begins
events.summary: Iraq invades Iran, beginning a war that will last nearly eight years and repeatedly threaten oil supplies.

events.headline: Pac-Man spreads beyond Japan
events.summary: Namco's Pac-Man begins its international rise, becoming one of the defining arcade games of the decade.

events.headline: Inflation remains a central election-year issue
events.summary: High consumer prices and borrowing costs continue to shape household finances and the presidential campaign.

events.headline: Philadelphia Phillies win the World Series
events.summary: The Phillies defeat the Kansas City Royals to win the franchise's first World Series championship.

events.headline: Carter and Reagan hold presidential debate
events.summary: The nationally televised debate becomes a defining moment in the closing days of the 1980 presidential campaign.

events.headline: Interest rates climb again
events.summary: After easing during the recession, U.S. interest rates rise sharply again as the Federal Reserve maintains its anti-inflation stance.

events.headline: Ronald Reagan wins U.S. presidential election
events.summary: Reagan defeats incumbent President Jimmy Carter in a decisive election victory.

events.headline: Voyager 1 flies past Saturn
events.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 makes its close encounter with Saturn, returning major scientific observations and images.

events.headline: Markets anticipate Reagan policy shift
events.summary: Investors begin positioning around expectations of tax cuts, deregulation, higher defense spending, and continued anti-inflation policy.

events.headline: John Lennon is murdered in New York
events.summary: Former Beatle John Lennon is shot and killed outside his Manhattan residence, prompting worldwide mourning.

events.headline: Federal funds rates approach extreme highs
events.summary: The Federal Reserve's inflation fight pushes short-term interest rates toward historically high levels.

events.headline: Home computing and video games gain momentum
events.summary: Personal computers, home consoles, and arcade games are becoming increasingly visible consumer technology categories entering the 1980s.

events.headline: Ronald Reagan inaugurated as 40th U.S. president
events.summary: Reagan takes office as the United States shifts toward tax cuts, deregulation, and increased defense spending.

events.headline: Iran releases 52 American hostages
events.summary: The Iran hostage crisis ends after 444 days, minutes after Reagan's inauguration.

events.headline: Oakland Raiders win Super Bowl XV
events.summary: The Raiders defeat the Philadelphia Eagles 27-10.

events.headline: Reagan presents economic program to Congress
events.summary: The administration outlines major tax and spending changes intended to reduce inflation and stimulate growth.

events.headline: Interest rates remain exceptionally high
events.summary: The Volcker Fed maintains tight monetary conditions as inflation remains a dominant policy concern.

events.headline: MTV preparations signal a changing music business
events.summary: Cable television and music-video programming are emerging as a new promotional channel ahead of MTV's launch later in the year.

events.headline: President Reagan survives assassination attempt
events.summary: John Hinckley Jr. shoots Reagan and several others outside a Washington hotel; Reagan survives.

events.headline: Ordinary People wins Best Picture
events.summary: The 53rd Academy Awards are held after a one-day delay caused by the Reagan shooting.

events.headline: High borrowing costs pressure housing and manufacturing
events.summary: Interest-sensitive sectors weaken under very tight monetary policy.

events.headline: Space Shuttle Columbia launches on STS-1
events.summary: NASA begins the Space Shuttle era with the first orbital flight of Columbia.

events.headline: Longest professional baseball game begins
events.summary: The Pawtucket Red Sox and Rochester Red Wings play into the 32nd inning before the game is suspended; it is completed in June.

events.headline: Reagan tax-cut push dominates policy debate
events.summary: Congress debates the administration's program of large reductions in marginal income-tax rates.

events.headline: American Airlines launches AAdvantage
events.summary: American Airlines introduces what becomes the first major modern frequent-flyer loyalty program.

events.headline: Japan adopts voluntary auto export restraints
events.summary: Japan limits automobile exports to the United States amid pressure over competition with U.S. automakers.

events.headline: Bob Marley dies
events.summary: Reggae icon Bob Marley dies at age 36, prompting global attention to his music and legacy.

events.headline: CDC reports unusual pneumonia cases later associated with AIDS
events.summary: A CDC report describes rare infections in young gay men, an early public milestone in recognition of the AIDS epidemic.

events.headline: Israel strikes Iraq's Osirak nuclear reactor
events.summary: Israeli aircraft destroy the Iraqi reactor near Baghdad in Operation Opera.

events.headline: Major League Baseball players strike
events.summary: An MLB labor dispute halts the season for nearly two months.

events.headline: U.S. enters the 1981-82 recession
events.summary: NBER later dates the business-cycle peak to July 1981 as tight monetary policy suppresses activity.

events.headline: Prince Charles and Lady Diana Spencer marry
events.summary: The royal wedding draws a massive worldwide television audience.

events.headline: Nintendo releases Donkey Kong
events.summary: Nintendo's arcade game introduces characters and gameplay that become foundational to its future game franchises.

events.headline: MTV begins broadcasting
events.summary: Music Television launches in the United States, accelerating the importance of music videos and cable youth culture.

events.headline: PATCO air traffic controllers strike
events.summary: President Reagan orders striking federal air traffic controllers back to work and later fires those who refuse.

events.headline: IBM Personal Computer introduced
events.summary: IBM launches the IBM PC, a milestone in the commercialization and standardization of personal computing.

events.headline: Economic Recovery Tax Act signed
events.summary: Reagan signs a major tax-cut package that reduces individual income-tax rates over several years.

events.headline: Sandra Day O'Connor confirmed to Supreme Court
events.summary: The Senate confirms O'Connor, who becomes the first woman to serve on the U.S. Supreme Court.

events.headline: Simon & Garfunkel perform in Central Park
events.summary: The reunion concert draws a huge crowd and becomes a major live-music event.

events.headline: Recessionary pressure spreads
events.summary: Manufacturing and other interest-sensitive industries weaken as the 1981-82 recession develops.

events.headline: First phase of Reagan income-tax cuts takes effect
events.summary: The initial reduction in the multi-stage federal income-tax cut becomes effective.

events.headline: Egyptian president Anwar Sadat assassinated
events.summary: Sadat is killed during a military parade, creating political uncertainty in a key Middle Eastern state.

events.headline: Los Angeles Dodgers win World Series
events.summary: The Dodgers defeat the New York Yankees four games to two.

events.headline: Space Shuttle Columbia flies STS-2
events.summary: The shuttle's second mission demonstrates reuse of an orbital spacecraft.

events.headline: Luke and Laura wedding draws huge TV audience
events.summary: The General Hospital wedding becomes one of the most-watched moments in daytime television history.

events.headline: U.S.-Soviet intermediate-range nuclear talks begin
events.summary: Negotiations open in Geneva over intermediate-range nuclear weapons in Europe.

events.headline: Martial law imposed in Poland
events.summary: Polish authorities impose martial law and move against the Solidarity movement.

events.headline: First American IVF baby born
events.summary: Elizabeth Jordan Carr is born in Virginia, marking a major U.S. milestone for in-vitro fertilization.

events.headline: Recession deepens into year-end
events.summary: High interest rates continue to suppress manufacturing, construction, and auto demand.

events.headline: AT&T agrees to break up Bell System
events.summary: The U.S. government and AT&T settle the antitrust case that will divide the Bell System into regional companies.

events.headline: Air Florida Flight 90 crashes in Washington
events.summary: The airliner crashes after takeoff into the 14th Street Bridge and Potomac River during severe winter weather.

events.headline: San Francisco 49ers win Super Bowl XVI
events.summary: The 49ers defeat the Cincinnati Bengals 26-21.

events.headline: Hama uprising is crushed
events.summary: Syrian government forces suppress an uprising in Hama with extensive casualties and destruction.

events.headline: Recession and high unemployment dominate
events.summary: The U.S. downturn continues under tight monetary conditions, with manufacturing and construction especially weak.

events.headline: Personal-computer software market expands
events.summary: The growing IBM PC ecosystem accelerates demand for business software and compatible hardware.

events.headline: United States bans Libyan oil imports
events.summary: The Reagan administration imposes an embargo on Libyan crude amid accusations of state support for terrorism.

events.headline: Chariots of Fire wins Best Picture
events.summary: The film wins Best Picture at the 54th Academy Awards.

events.headline: Volcker disinflation continues
events.summary: Inflation is falling, but the cost is severe weakness in employment and output.

events.headline: Argentina invades Falkland Islands
events.summary: Argentine forces seize the islands, triggering the Falklands War with the United Kingdom.

events.headline: Major April blizzard hits northeastern United States
events.summary: A powerful spring snowstorm disrupts travel, schools, businesses, and baseball schedules.

events.headline: Housing and auto sectors remain under heavy pressure
events.summary: High financing costs continue to depress major interest-sensitive industries.

events.headline: 1982 World's Fair opens in Knoxville
events.summary: The World's Fair opens and ultimately attracts more than 11 million visitors.

events.headline: The Weather Channel launches
events.summary: The first 24-hour U.S. television weather network begins broadcasting.

events.headline: Braniff International Airways ceases operations
events.summary: Financially troubled Braniff files for bankruptcy and stops flying.

events.headline: Falklands War intensifies
events.summary: British and Argentine forces fight at sea and in the islands, including the sinking of General Belgrano and loss of HMS Sheffield.

events.headline: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial opens
events.summary: Steven Spielberg's film becomes a major box-office phenomenon and one of the defining movies of the decade.

events.headline: Argentina surrenders in Falklands War
events.summary: Argentine forces surrender in the Falkland Islands, effectively ending the conflict.

events.headline: Los Angeles Lakers win NBA championship
events.summary: The Lakers defeat the Philadelphia 76ers in the NBA Finals.

events.headline: Italy wins FIFA World Cup
events.summary: Italy defeats West Germany 3-1 in Madrid to win the World Cup.

events.headline: Federal Reserve begins backing away from extreme monetary restraint
events.summary: With the recession severe and inflation falling, monetary policy starts becoming less restrictive.

events.headline: TRON showcases computer-generated imagery
events.summary: Disney's TRON becomes a notable early use of extensive computer imagery in a feature film.

events.headline: Mexico signals debt crisis
events.summary: Mexico announces it can no longer meet scheduled debt payments, helping trigger the Latin American debt crisis.

events.headline: PLO evacuation from Beirut begins
events.summary: Palestine Liberation Organization forces begin leaving Beirut after the Israeli invasion of Lebanon.

events.headline: Long-term interest rates begin a major decline
events.summary: As inflation expectations ease and the Fed shifts, bond yields begin falling from historic highs.

events.headline: First widely recognized emoticons are proposed online
events.summary: Scott Fahlman suggests :-) and :-( in an online message-board discussion.

events.headline: NFL players begin 57-day strike
events.summary: The strike reduces the regular season to nine games and forces an expanded playoff format.

events.headline: Chicago Tylenol murders begin
events.summary: Cyanide-laced Tylenol capsules kill seven people and lead to sweeping changes in consumer-product packaging.

events.headline: EPCOT Center opens at Walt Disney World
events.summary: Disney opens its second Florida theme park, focused on technology, culture, and international pavilions.

events.headline: Garn-St Germain Depository Institutions Act signed
events.summary: The law accelerates financial deregulation and gives thrift institutions broader lending powers.

events.headline: Inflation falls sharply
events.summary: Year-over-year inflation drops substantially from its 1980 peak as the recession and tight policy suppress price pressures.

events.headline: 1981-82 recession reaches its trough
events.summary: NBER later dates November 1982 as the end of the severe recession.

events.headline: Vietnam Veterans Memorial dedicated
events.summary: The memorial is formally dedicated in Washington, D.C.

events.headline: Michael Jackson releases Thriller
events.summary: Thriller is released and goes on to become one of the most commercially successful albums in history.

events.headline: First permanent artificial heart implanted
events.summary: Barney Clark receives the Jarvik-7 artificial heart in Utah.

events.headline: Unemployment peaks near 11 percent
events.summary: U.S. unemployment reaches about 10.8 percent around the end of the recession, the highest level of the postwar era to that point.

events.headline: Time names the computer its Machine of the Year
events.summary: Time magazine selects the personal computer rather than a person, highlighting computing's growing cultural and economic importance.

events.headline: ARPANET completes transition to TCP/IP
events.summary: The network formally adopts TCP/IP, a milestone often associated with the birth of the modern Internet.

events.headline: Apple introduces Lisa computer
events.summary: Apple releases the Lisa, notable for bringing a graphical user interface and mouse to a commercial personal computer.

events.headline: Lotus 1-2-3 released
events.summary: Lotus launches its spreadsheet software for IBM-compatible PCs, quickly becoming a major business application.

events.headline: Washington wins Super Bowl XVII
events.summary: Washington defeats the Miami Dolphins 27-17.

events.headline: Federal government announces Times Beach buyout
events.summary: The EPA plans evacuation and purchase of the dioxin-contaminated Missouri community.

events.headline: M*A*S*H finale draws enormous television audience
events.summary: The final episode of M*A*S*H becomes one of the most-watched U.S. television broadcasts ever.

events.headline: Recovery begins to strengthen
events.summary: Following the November 1982 trough, falling interest rates and improving demand support an accelerating U.S. recovery.

events.headline: IBM releases PC XT
events.summary: IBM expands its personal-computer line with the PC XT, including a built-in hard drive.

events.headline: Reagan announces Strategic Defense Initiative
events.summary: President Reagan proposes research into missile-defense systems, quickly nicknamed 'Star Wars.'

events.headline: Michael Jackson performs moonwalk during Motown 25 taping
events.summary: The performance of 'Billie Jean,' broadcast later in May, becomes a defining moment in Jackson's rise.

events.headline: Space Shuttle Challenger launches on STS-6
events.summary: Challenger begins its first mission; the flight includes the first U.S. spacewalk of the shuttle program.

events.headline: Tokyo Disneyland opens
events.summary: Disney's first theme park outside the United States opens near Tokyo.

events.headline: Interest-sensitive sectors rebound
events.summary: Lower rates help housing and automobile demand recover strongly from the 1981-82 recession.

events.headline: Motown 25 airs on television
events.summary: The anniversary special broadcasts Michael Jackson's celebrated 'Billie Jean' performance to a national audience.

events.headline: Return of the Jedi opens
events.summary: The third released Star Wars film becomes one of the year's biggest entertainment events.

events.headline: Economic expansion gains pace
events.summary: Consumer spending, housing, and production improve rapidly during the first full year of recovery.

events.headline: Sally Ride becomes first American woman in space
events.summary: Ride launches aboard Space Shuttle Challenger on STS-7.

events.headline: WarGames brings computer hacking into popular culture
events.summary: The film WarGames popularizes public awareness of computers, networks, hacking, and nuclear-command risks.

events.headline: U.S. recovery broadens
events.summary: Employment and production continue improving as inflation remains much lower than at the start of the decade.

events.headline: NBER announces the 1981-82 recession ended in November 1982
events.summary: The Business Cycle Dating Committee formally identifies the prior November as the recession trough.

events.headline: Nintendo launches Famicom
events.summary: Nintendo releases the Family Computer console in Japan, the platform later adapted as the Nintendo Entertainment System.

events.headline: Black July violence begins
events.summary: Anti-Tamil riots in Sri Lanka intensify the country's ethnic conflict and civil war.

events.headline: Hurricane Alicia strikes Texas
events.summary: Alicia hits the Houston-Galveston region, causing major damage and disruption.

events.headline: Strong recovery boosts consumer demand
events.summary: Falling inflation and improved employment support stronger spending and business activity.

events.headline: Personal computer competition intensifies
events.summary: IBM-compatible PCs, Apple systems, and rapidly growing software markets make personal computing a mainstream business story.

events.headline: Soviet forces shoot down Korean Air Lines Flight 007
events.summary: The civilian Boeing 747 is destroyed after entering Soviet airspace, killing all 269 people aboard and sharply worsening Cold War tensions.

events.headline: Vanessa Williams becomes first Black Miss America
events.summary: Williams wins the Miss America title, a major cultural milestone in the pageant's history.

events.headline: GPS access becomes part of post-KAL 007 policy discussion
events.summary: The Reagan administration moves toward making satellite navigation available for civilian use once the system is operational.

events.headline: Beirut barracks bombing kills U.S. and French personnel
events.summary: Truck bombs strike multinational-force barracks in Beirut, killing hundreds, including 241 U.S. service members.

events.headline: United States invades Grenada
events.summary: U.S. and allied forces land in Grenada following political upheaval on the island.

events.headline: Microsoft Word enters the PC software market
events.summary: Microsoft releases the first version of Word for MS-DOS, adding to competition in personal-computer productivity software.

events.headline: Able Archer 83 NATO exercise begins
events.summary: A NATO command exercise is interpreted with unusual concern by Soviet leaders, becoming one of the tense moments of the late Cold War.

events.headline: The Day After airs on ABC
events.summary: The television film depicting nuclear war draws an enormous audience and intensifies public debate about nuclear weapons.

events.headline: Recovery drives rapid job growth
events.summary: The economy continues expanding strongly a year after the recession trough.

events.headline: Australia floats its dollar
events.summary: The Australian government allows the currency to float and liberalizes foreign-exchange controls.

events.headline: Democracy returns to Argentina
events.summary: Raul Alfonsin takes office, ending years of military rule.

events.headline: Harrods bombing in London
events.summary: An IRA car bomb outside Harrods kills six people and injures dozens.

events.headline: Bell System breakup takes effect
events.summary: AT&T's local telephone operations are separated into regional Bell companies, reshaping U.S. telecommunications.

events.headline: Van Halen releases 1984
events.summary: The album becomes a major commercial hit, led by singles including 'Jump.'

events.headline: Apple launches Macintosh
events.summary: Steve Jobs introduces the Macintosh, bringing a graphical interface and mouse-driven computing to a mass audience.

events.headline: First untethered spacewalk
events.summary: Astronaut Bruce McCandless II flies freely from Space Shuttle Challenger using the Manned Maneuvering Unit.

events.headline: Sarajevo Winter Olympics begin
events.summary: The Winter Games open in Yugoslavia and run through February 19.

events.headline: Michael Jackson wins eight Grammy Awards
events.summary: Jackson sets a single-night Grammy record during the peak of Thriller's cultural impact.

events.headline: British miners' strike begins
events.summary: The National Union of Mineworkers launches a prolonged strike over planned coal-mine closures.

events.headline: UN condemns chemical weapons use in Iran-Iraq War
events.summary: International concern rises over Iraq's use of chemical weapons during the war with Iran.

events.headline: Expansion remains strong as inflation stays moderate
events.summary: The U.S. economy continues its powerful post-recession expansion with improving labor markets and lower inflation than in 1980-82.

events.headline: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar becomes NBA all-time scoring leader
events.summary: Abdul-Jabbar passes Wilt Chamberlain's career scoring record.

events.headline: India launches Operation Meghdoot
events.summary: Indian forces occupy key positions on the Siachen Glacier, beginning the long-running Siachen conflict.

events.headline: Terms of Endearment leads Academy Awards
events.summary: The film wins Best Picture and multiple major awards at the 56th Academy Awards.

events.headline: Itaipu Dam begins generating electricity
events.summary: The massive hydroelectric project on the Brazil-Paraguay border starts power generation.

events.headline: Soviet Union announces Los Angeles Olympics boycott
events.summary: The USSR says it will not participate in the 1984 Summer Olympics, followed by many allied states.

events.headline: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom opens
events.summary: The film becomes a major summer hit and helps shape the modern blockbuster era.

events.headline: Operation Blue Star begins
events.summary: Indian forces enter the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar in an operation against Sikh militants.

events.headline: Ghostbusters and Gremlins open
events.summary: Two influential 1980s films debut on the same day and become major commercial successes.

events.headline: Boston Celtics win NBA championship
events.summary: The Celtics defeat the Los Angeles Lakers in a seven-game NBA Finals series.

events.headline: Geraldine Ferraro selected as Democratic VP nominee
events.summary: Walter Mondale chooses Ferraro, the first woman nominated for vice president by a major U.S. political party.

events.headline: Los Angeles Summer Olympics begin
events.summary: The 1984 Summer Games open in Los Angeles amid a Soviet-led boycott.

events.headline: Purple Rain film opens
events.summary: Prince's Purple Rain reaches theaters during the album's breakthrough cultural moment.

events.headline: Los Angeles Olympics conclude
events.summary: The Games close after a commercially successful Olympics for Los Angeles and the United States.

events.headline: Strong expansion continues into late summer
events.summary: Growth remains robust, though interest-rate and deficit concerns stay prominent in markets and policy debate.

events.headline: Personal computers become a mainstream consumer battleground
events.summary: Apple, IBM, Commodore and compatible-PC makers compete for a rapidly expanding home and business computer market.

events.headline: Brian Mulroney wins Canadian federal election
events.summary: The Progressive Conservatives win a large parliamentary majority, ending years of Liberal dominance.

events.headline: First MTV Video Music Awards held
events.summary: MTV stages the inaugural VMAs, reflecting the growing influence of music video culture.

events.headline: Reagan-Mondale general election campaign intensifies
events.summary: The presidential campaign moves into its fall phase with the economy and Cold War policy central issues.

events.headline: Brighton hotel bombing targets British government
events.summary: An IRA bomb strikes the Grand Hotel during the Conservative Party conference; Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher survives.

events.headline: Detroit Tigers win World Series
events.summary: The Tigers defeat the San Diego Padres four games to one.

events.headline: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi assassinated
events.summary: Gandhi is killed by two of her bodyguards, followed by severe anti-Sikh violence.

events.headline: Ronald Reagan wins landslide re-election
events.summary: Reagan defeats Walter Mondale, carrying 49 states and winning 525 electoral votes.

events.headline: A Nightmare on Elm Street opens
events.summary: The horror film introduces Freddy Krueger and becomes an enduring franchise.

events.headline: Band Aid records Do They Know It's Christmas?
events.summary: British and Irish music stars record a charity single to raise funds for Ethiopian famine relief.

events.headline: Bhopal gas disaster
events.summary: A toxic gas leak at a Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal kills thousands and becomes one of history's worst industrial disasters.

events.headline: Ethiopian famine drives global relief attention
events.summary: Television coverage and charity efforts make the Ethiopian famine a major international humanitarian issue.

events.headline: U.S. completes a strong expansion year
events.summary: The post-1982 recovery delivers strong growth and declining unemployment, while federal deficits remain a policy concern.
